Food Safety

Food safety — food-borne illnesses, safe handling, storage and prevention of contamination.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • State the principles of food safety
  • Describe safe food handling and storage
  • Explain how to prevent food-borne illness

In simple words

Food safety means handling, preparing and storing food so that it does not cause illness. Unsafe food can carry germs and cause diarrhoea, vomiting and food poisoning.

The key principles are: keep clean, separate raw and cooked food, cook thoroughly, keep food at safe temperatures, and use safe water and raw materials.

Five keys to safer food (WHO)

Key What to do
Keep clean Wash hands, surfaces and utensils
Separate raw and cooked Use separate boards and knives
Cook thoroughly Heat food to kill germs
Keep at safe temperatures Refrigerate perishables; serve hot food hot
Use safe water and raw materials Use clean water; wash fruits and vegetables

Food-borne illness

Common causes: bacteria (Salmonella, E. coli), viruses, parasites, toxins. Symptoms: nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, fever.

Prevention: hand hygiene, safe cooking, safe storage, clean water, excluding sick food handlers.

🔴 Five keys to safer food

Keep clean, separate raw and cooked, cook thoroughly, keep at safe temperatures, use safe water and raw materials.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Patient food — ensure hospital food is freshly cooked, covered and served at safe temperatures.
  • Health teaching — teach hand washing before eating and after toilet; safe food storage at home.
  • Food-borne illness — suspect it when vomiting and diarrhoea occur after a common meal; report outbreaks.
  • Vulnerable groups — children, pregnant women and elderly are at higher risk; be extra careful.
  • Kitchen hygiene — support clean kitchens, safe water and healthy food handlers.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Food safety prevents food-borne illness from germs and toxins.
  2. Five keys: keep clean, separate raw/cooked, cook thoroughly, safe temperatures, safe water/materials.
  3. Symptoms: nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, fever.
  4. Hand washing before eating and after toilet prevents spread.
  5. Vulnerable groups: children, pregnant women, elderly.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Reheat cooked food only once.
  2. Store perishables in the refrigerator; serve hot food hot.
  3. Wash fruits and vegetables before eating.
  4. Exclude sick people from handling food.

📌 Memory trick

Five keys: “C-S-C-T-S” — Clean, Separate, Cook, Temperature, Safe water/materials.

60-second revision

  • Food safety = safe handling, preparation, storage.
  • Five keys: clean, separate, cook, temperature, safe water.
  • Symptoms: vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, fever.
  • Hand washing before eating prevents illness.
  • Reheat food only once; refrigerate perishables.

Test yourself

Which is NOT one of the five keys to safer food?

Answer: D. Eating only raw food is not a safety key; cooking thoroughly kills germs.

Food-borne illness symptoms include:

Answer: B. Vomiting and diarrhoea are common food-borne illness symptoms.

Raw and cooked food should be:

Answer: B. Separating raw and cooked food prevents cross-contamination.

Cooked food should be reheated:

Answer: B. Reheat cooked food only once to reduce microbial growth risk.

Who is at higher risk from food-borne illness?

Answer: B. Children, pregnant women and elderly people are more vulnerable.
